grammarQuestions.q: It’s Saturday tomorrow and there’s no school, so I ______ wake up early.
feedback: There’s no school, so it isn’t necessary.
There’s no school, so you are free.
Waking up early isn’t against the rules.

grammarQuestions.q: Students ______ use their phones during the exam. It’s against the rules.
feedback: It’s a rule, so this isn’t the right meaning.
This is advice, but this sentence is about a rule.
Phones are not allowed in the exam.

grammarQuestions.q: Excuse me, ______ I open the window, please?
feedback: We don’t ask for permission with mustn’t.
We don’t ask for permission with have to.
We say I don’t, not I doesn’t.

grammarQuestions.q:
Ece is visiting Ali’s house for the first time. There are pet beds in every room, cat toys on the sofa, and a big bird cage next to the window. On the wall, there is a poster: “Adopt, don’t shop!”
Ece: “Wow, Ali ______ love animals!”
feedback: Mustn’t means something is not allowed. Here, the pet beds, toys and cage give us clues about Ali.
Can’t would mean it is not possible. These clues strongly suggest that Ali loves animals.
Doesn’t have to means it is not necessary. Ece is making a conclusion from the clues, not talking about a duty.

grammarQuestions.q:
At the school gate, Mert points at a tall boy with a red backpack.
Mert: “Look, Ayşe! Is that your brother?”
Ayşe: “Haha, no! I only have two sisters.”
Mert: “Oh, right. That boy ______ be her brother.”
feedback: Must would mean we are sure he is her brother. Ayşe says she only has sisters, so he cannot be her brother.
Might means it is possible. Ayşe only has sisters, so this is not possible.
Should gives advice or an expectation. Here, Mert knows from Ayşe’s words that the boy cannot be her brother.
